ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within the rhombus $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and their lengths are $6\text{cm}$ and $8\text{cm}$, respectively. A line passing through point $O$ intersects $AD$ and $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. What is the sum of the areas of the shaded regions in $\text{cm}^2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AC$ and $BD$ are the diagonals of the rhombus $ABCD$,\\
it follows that $AC \perp BD$, and $OA=OC$, $AD\parallel BC$,\\
therefore, $\angle OAE=\angle OCF$, $\angle AEO=\angle CFO$,\\
thus, $\triangle AOE\cong \triangle COF$,\\
hence, the areas are $S_{\triangle AOE}=S_{\triangle COF}$,\\
therefore, $S_{\text{shaded}}=S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\text{rhombus} ABCD}$,\\
Given the lengths of the diagonals of the rhombus are 6cm and 8cm,\\
which means: $S_{\text{shaded}}=S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\text{rhombus} ABCD}=\frac{1}{2}\times (\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8)=\boxed{12}\text{cm}^2$

Solve to get \(E=\left(\frac{12}{3+4k},\frac{12k}{3+4k}\right)\) and \(F=-E\). 推理：按指定坐标法，以 O 为原点放置菱形，令 A=(0,3)，C=(0,-3)，B=(-4,0)，D=(4,0)，这样 AC=6，BD=8。设过 O 的直线为 y=kx。边 AD 过 A、D，方程为 3x+4y=12；边 BC 过 B、C，方程为 3x+4y=-12。与 y=kx 联立，得 E=(12/(3+4k), 12k/(3+4k))，而 F=-E。由于 E、F 在相应边段上，k≥0。

用行列式面积公式：
[AOE]=1/2|det(A,E)|=1/2|0·y_E-3x_E|=18/(3+4k)。
[BOF]=1/2|det(B,F)|。因 F=(-x_E,-y_E)，所以 [BOF]=1/2|(-4)(-y_E)|=2y_E=24k/(3+4k)。
因此 [AOE]+[BOF]=(18+24k)/(3+4k)=6。

又 [ODC]=1/2|det(D,C)|=1/2|4·(-3)-0·0|=6。

所以阴影面积和为 6+6=12 cm²。

用行列式面积公式：
[AOE]=1/2|det(A,E)|=1/2|0·y_E-3x_E|=18/(3+4k)。
[BOF]=1/2|det(B,F)|。因 F=(-x_E,-y_E)，所以 [BOF]=1/2|(-4)(-y_E)|=2y_E=24k/(3+4k)。
因此 [AOE]+[BOF]=(18+24k)/(3+4k)=6。

又 [ODC]=1/2|det(D,C)|=1/2|4·(-3)-0·0|=6。

所以阴影面积和为 6+6=12 cm²。

raw_record.original_question: Within the rhombus $ABCD$, the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and their lengths are $6\text{cm}$ and $8\text{cm}$, respectively. A line passing through point $O$ intersects $AD$ and $BC$ at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. What is the sum of the areas of the shaded regions in $\text{cm}^2$?
raw_record.answer: Since $AC$ and $BD$ are the diagonals of the rhombus $ABCD$, it follows that $AC \perp BD$, and $OA=OC$, $AD\parallel BC$. Therefore, $\angle OAE=\angle OCF$, $\angle AEO=\angle CFO$, thus, $\triangle AOE\cong \triangle COF$, hence, the areas are $S_{\triangle AOE}=S_{\triangle COF}$. Therefore, $S_{\text{shaded}}=S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\text{rhombus }ABCD}$. Given the lengths of the diagonals of the rhombus are 6cm and 8cm, we get $S_{\text{shaded}}=S_{\triangle BCD}=\frac{1}{2}S_{\text{rhombus }ABCD}=\frac{1}{2}\times \left(\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 8\right)=\boxed{12}\text{cm}^2$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is rhombus ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right; diagonals AC and BD intersect at O. There is also a line segment EF passing through O, E is on AD, F is on BC. The shaded parts include the small upper-left triangle AOE, the lower triangle BOF, and the right-side triangle ODC; the unshaded triangle COF is between BOF and ODC.
Reasoning: Because ABCD is a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other, obtaining OA=OC, and AD∥BC. Since A,O,C are collinear, E,O,F are collinear, and AE∥CF, ∠OAE=∠OCF, ∠AEO=∠CFO. Therefore △AOE≅△COF, and the areas are equal. Replace the shaded △AOE with the equal-area △COF, then the total shaded area equals △BOF+△COF+△ODC, which is the area of △BCD. △BCD is half of rhombus ABCD. The area of the rhombus is (1/2)×AC×BD=(1/2)×6×8=24, so the sum of the shaded areas is 24÷2=12.
